scientific_conclusion: The exact Stage-80 node-21 field is reconstructed from all 96 already-fixed angular ordinates to machine precision. No single ordinate reaches the preregistered 5% cell-divergence dominance guard (the largest is ordinate 20 at 75 degrees with 3.3140%), and the top twelve ordinates carry only 36.7021%, below the 50% cluster guard. In contrast, the inherited vertical-oblique sectors [1,2,5,6] carry 88.6792% of the node-level cell-divergence magnitude, exceeding the fixed 70% sector-concentration guard. Opposite-ordinate pairing retains 99.8149% of cell-divergence magnitude and 96.7979% of face magnitude, so individual opposite directions do not explain the global cancellation. These are frozen residual-structure diagnostics only: they are not adjoint sensitivities, do not justify velocity-rule modification, and do not rehabilitate the failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint.
positive_findings: All 96 fixed angular ordinates on the exact Stage-80 dominant radial node are resolved and reconstruct every inherited angular-bin map to numerical precision.
The vertical-oblique sectors carry 88.6792% of the node-level cell-divergence magnitude, providing a preregistered reason to inspect within-sector angular coherence next.
No cavity solver rerun or physical/numerical retuning was performed.
negative_findings: The largest individual ordinate carries only 3.3140% and the top twelve only 36.7021%, so there is no supported single-ordinate or compact-ordinate-cluster explanation.
Individual-ordinate prominence is not an adjoint sensitivity and is not evidence that pruning, moving, or reweighting velocity ordinates would improve q_av.
The exact inherited Stage-80 angular-bin labels are preserved despite non-nominal boundary counts; Stage 81 does not rebucket the velocity rule.
The failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint remains unrecovered and is not extended across Knudsen number; no validation claim is made.
